title: You didn’t post that for connection. You posted it to be seen.
paragraphs: You didn’t post that for connection. You posted it to be seen.
And deep down… you knew it.
The lighting was perfect. The caption was crafted just enough to sound effortless. You checked it once. Then again. Then ten more times. Watching the numbers climb like your worth was tied to it.
God saw it.
Not just the post—the motive behind it.
Because here’s what most people don’t realize… social media doesn’t just reveal influence. It exposes the heart.
It can be a tool. Or it can be a mirror you’re addicted to.

At first, it feels harmless. You tell yourself you’re sharing your life, your thoughts, your creativity. And maybe you are. But slowly, something shifts. The question is no longer “Is this true?” or “Is this helpful?” It becomes “Will this perform?”
And that’s where it starts feeding something darker.
Your ego.
You begin curating, not expressing. Performing, not living. Measuring your value in reactions instead of truth. And when the response is low, something inside you sinks. Not because the post failed…
But because you feel like you did.
You won’t say it out loud. But you feel it.
God saw it.
The quiet comparison when someone else’s post did better.
The subtle jealousy when they gained followers faster.
The way you smiled publicly but wrestled privately.
You knew.
Scripture doesn’t ignore this. It cuts straight through it.
“Am I now seeking the approval of man, or of God? Or am I trying to please man? If I were still trying to please man, I would not be a servant of Christ.” — Galatians 1:10
Read that again.
Because that verse doesn’t leave room for negotiation. It draws a line.
You can build influence for God… or you can build a platform for yourself. But the two are not the same, no matter how similar they look on the surface.
And that’s where it gets dangerous.
Because you can use the name of Jesus and still be feeding your ego.
You can post Bible verses and still crave validation more than transformation.
You can talk about truth while being enslaved to opinions.
That tension inside you? That pull between wanting to be seen and wanting to be real?
That’s not random.
That’s a battle for your soul.
Jesus didn’t avoid this topic. He confronted it directly.
“Beware of practicing your righteousness before other people in order to be seen by them… for then you will have no reward from your Father who is in heaven.” — Matthew 6:1
He didn’t say don’t do good things.
He said check why you’re doing them.
Because the same action can either glorify God… or glorify you.
And one of those leads to life.
The other leads to emptiness.
You’ve felt that emptiness, haven’t you?
The moment after the post peaks.
The silence when engagement fades.
The strange hollowness after chasing attention and actually getting it.
Because attention was never meant to satisfy your soul.
Only God can do that.
But sin twists that desire. It tells you that if enough people see you, affirm you, follow you… then you’ll finally feel secure.
But it never lasts.
It just resets the craving.
More likes.
More reach.
More validation.
And suddenly, you’re not using social media.
It’s using you.
You’re not building influence.
You’re feeding an idol.
And Scripture calls that what it is.
Idolatry isn’t just statues and rituals. It’s anything you elevate to give you identity, worth, or security apart from God.
Even your image.
Even your platform.
Even your “influence.”
But here’s the truth that cuts through all of it.
You don’t need to be seen by the world to be known by God.
“And your Father who sees in secret will reward you.” — Matthew 6:4
He sees what no algorithm can measure.
He sees your motives.
Your struggles.
Your private battles.
Your real self.
And He doesn’t offer you likes.
He offers you grace.
Because the Gospel isn’t about building your name.
It’s about surrendering it.
You are not saved by your platform, your content, or your influence.
You are saved by Jesus Christ—His life, His death, His resurrection.
“For by grace you have been saved through faith. And this is not your own doing; it is the gift of God.” — Ephesians 2:8
That means you don’t have to perform anymore.
You don’t have to prove yourself.
You don’t have to chase validation from people who can’t save you.
You can be free.
Free to post without pretending.
Free to step back without fear.
Free to speak truth even if it doesn’t trend.
Free to live for an audience of One.
But that freedom requires something most people avoid.
Repentance.
A turning away from the need to be seen… and a turning toward the God who already sees you fully.
No filters.
No edits.
No performance.
Just truth.
So now the question isn’t whether social media is good or bad.
The question is… what is it doing to you?
Is it drawing you closer to truth?
Or deeper into performance?
Is it making you bold for Christ?
Or dependent on approval?
Be honest.
God already knows the answer.
And right now, you’re standing at a quiet crossroads.
One path keeps feeding the ego.
The other leads to surrender… and real life.
Say it plainly.
“I’ve been doing it for attention.”
“I’ve been chasing validation.”
“I need God more than I need approval.”
Write it. Own it.
And if you know someone who’s trapped in this same cycle, don’t stay silent. Send this to them. Because silence keeps people stuck.
There’s more depth waiting for you. More truth that will challenge, expose, and rebuild you the right way. That’s what you step into when you go deeper.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior.
